name: Small-scale Ecosystem Grants
summary: Grants for small on-the-ground projects of two years or less that restore wetlands, riparian areas, fish habitat, forests or grasslands, or conserve species of concern, in the Columbia Basin of British Columbia. Intake is continuous until funds run out.

amount.note: Typical maximum Trust funding per project, not counting wage subsidy

steps: Discuss project idea with Columbia Basin Trust
Submit full online application, if invited

eligibility.rule: Applicants outside the Basin partner with a Basin community organisation and show benefits for the Basin
Project takes place on Crown, local government, First Nations or conservation land
Site is outside private holdings, BC Hydro or Fortis land, and provincial or federal parks
Includes on-the-ground work with measurable local ecological benefits
Work has no potential to duplicate or displace government or industry responsibilities
Work does not displace or harm existing tenure holders, licensees or permitted users
Project does not primarily benefit the applicant or, for a membership organisation, its members

status.quote: Applications are accepted on a first-received, first-served basis and are assessed as they come in and continue until all funding for the program has been committed.

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include registered non-profits, local governments and First Nations in the Columbia Basin Trust region

geography.quote: Eligible applicants include registered non-profits, local governments and First Nations in the Columbia Basin Trust region

access.quote: Contact ecosystems@ourtrust.org to enquire about your project. Eligible projects will be invited to apply and sent an application form.

window.quote: The Small-scale Ecosystems Grants accepts inquiries and applications on a continuous basis throughout the year.

amount.quote: The typical maximum amount of Trust funding for any one project is $80,000, not including wage subsidy funding.

co_finance_required.quote: Up to 80% of total project costs can be requested from the Trust.

effort.quote: If you are an eligible applicant interested in applying, contact ecosystems@ourtrust.org to discuss your project idea with us.
If your project meets the program criteria, you will be invited to submit an online application.
The review process for submitted applications usually takes up to eight weeks.

eligibility.quote: Eligible applicants include registered non-profits, local governments and First Nations in the Columbia Basin Trust region (ourtrust.org/map).
Applicants operating outside the Basin must partner with community-based organizations operating within the region and must show that the project benefits the Basin.
take place on crown land, local government land, First Nations land, or conservation land
take place on personally or commercially held private land, BC Hydro or Fortis land, or Provincial/Federal Parks
have on-the-ground action (rather than strictly research, education or planning) to support ecological health and resilience at a local level that yield meaningful and measurable benefits
have the potential to duplicate or displace government or industry responsibility.
displace or negatively impact existing tenure holders, licensees and/or permitted users
primarily benefit the applicant itself or the members of a membership-based organization

co_finance.quote: The application should clearly demonstrate that at least 20% of total project costs will be received from sources other than the Trust, and that 50% of wage and MERCs costs will be paid by the employer.
